title: Lion, Totem of the White Howlers
summary: The proud tribal totem of the lost tribe.

claims.text: Lion is proud and strong: a skilled tracker, a hard fighter and a noble leader whose charges stay safe while Lion walks.
Lion shows no mercy to anyone who invades the territory, claims the mantle or harasses those under Lion's care.
Some who hear of Lion's patronage are puzzled, linking the name to the African great cat rather than this northern spirit.

title: The White Howlers in Caledonia
summary: The tribe's homeland and its neighbours in the north.

claims.text: Tribal memory holds that the Great Winter's ice drove the tribe's ancestors south; their septs were spread so thinly across the Caledonian wilds that finding an unknown sept of the tribe was common.
Meeting werewolves who did not follow Lion was another matter, and the ways of the Children of Stag still seem strange to White Howlers.

title: The Picts
summary: The human people the White Howlers watched over.

claims.text: Popular images of the Picts as small, blue-painted, half-fae barbarians with poisoned spears hold grains of truth but are far from fair or accurate as a whole.
At the tribe's height the White Howlers' Kinfolk were among the Picts.
A White Howler born to Kinfolk parents who had long forgotten their werewolf ties would be nearly impossible, but such a birth would draw the spirits' notice, Lion's above all.

title: The White Howlers' War with Rome
summary: How fighting the legions left the tribe's Kin open to corruption.

claims.text: The tribe learned that meeting the Roman legions head on was hopeless, since its Kinfolk lacked the training and resources to stand against them.
Busy settling back into the homeland after the Great Winter, the tribe noticed its Kinfolk's skirmishes with Rome almost too late.

While the shapeshifters were away campaigning against Rome, fomori serving the invaders struck the undefended Kinfolk; survivors carried the taint of the attack in mind and blood, and some became fomori themselves.
Rome's northern walls include the Antonine Wall, begun in AD 142 under Emperor Antoninus.
